chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Clef Club finances, the $1,500 rent and hotels paying to keep it closed
summary: Rent and charter fees ran $1,000 a month covered by $5 memberships; after the win the landlord demanded $1,500 rent, and Horace says six downtown hotels paid him $100,000 each to keep it shut.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And we won the case, and I'll inject a little financial thing here. We were paying rent down to an agency here that owned a lot of buildings, Dikreau the building. It's called the Review Realty. He was renting us this place for his -- for $750.00 a month. We were playing -- paying $250.00 a month to the Rudensky Foundation for the use of the charter. That was $1,000.00 a month. And because of the fact that we couldn't sell whiskey, we had to charge for membership. We You could get a card for $5.00. First we started out at $3.00, and then we

went up to 5.00. We had 3,500 members. Okay. So all you would pay for there would be your setups, and, of course, we had a food deal affair where we sold the tacos and whatnot which (unintelligible). It helped keep the people happy, after they got hungry. (Unintelligible). They wanted the tacos and they'd have their own drinks, you know. We would -- if they wanted 7-Up, or one of those things, we could get that, you know.

So that worked out real good. But we went to court -- here's the pathetic thing -- and won the case, we went back to reopen. We could have opened. Dikeou Tekiew, the real estate agency that owned the building, wanted $1,500.00 rent. There was no way that we could meet that.

Because we still didn't have a whiskey license. (unintelligible). But we didn't know why the guy went up on us until, oh, a couple of months later, but we found out later, and this is still going on right now what I'm going to say. We found out later that there were six major hotels downtown paying him -- they got together and paid him $100,000.00 each to keep the Clef (unintelligible) Club closed. So he figured that -- well, he'd get $600,000.00 a month for nothing, one of those things, and now the pigeons have it, (unintelligible) has this affair stirred up, But he regrets it, because he saw Bob Carr about, oh, a year ago and wanted to know if he wanted it back. Bob Carr told him in no uncertain terms that -- what he could do with it. Because after he had found out

we found out, you know... (unintelligible). But we found out also the reason that he was so anxious to have us take it back again, because some of the $100.00 a month guys were dropping out. They figured they'd gained their point by now, and the building was out of shape. It was out of the people's minds, one of those things, so this is the story of the Clef Club. It was really pathetic (unintelligible).
Uh-huh. Now one thing I might say, this is on tape here, and if you want, I know that the Smithsonian people will delete it, if you would prefer that.
Because it could be -- we could get into a thing there;
Yes, if you could (unintelligible), well, it's all right with me if they would.
You prefer they delete it or leave it on?
Well, that's up to them. It gives the actual facts, and I don't think we've called any of those major hotels' names.
